title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on network routing issues observed during benchmark runs, plan for runtime upgrade to v2.2.0-rc1, confirming next steps for VPC peering and audit log access. Customer requested a short latency run and security doc bundle; Redwood to provide runbook and updated deployment manifest.
topics: Networking: VPC peering, routing, NAT/GW flows
Benchmark results and tail latency spikes
action_items: Samir Patel: Share updated network runbook and VPC peering checklist by 2026-12-04
Jessica Hu: Schedule 30-min latency benchmark run with Aaron and Ethan for 2026-12-06
Diego Alvarez: Prepare v2.2.0-rc1 rollout notes and rollback plan by 2026-12-05
Priya Singh: Provide list of required audit log fields and retention policy feedback by 2026-12-07
next_steps: Redwood to run a focused 1-hour latency benchmark during low-traffic window (target 2026-12-06)
Customer to confirm VPC peering CIDR ranges and request temporary NAT/GW rule change

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-02 15:00 UTC · duration 42m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jessica (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Platform), Marta (Atlas ML), Ethan (Atlas Infra), Priya (Atlas Security), Aaron (Atlas DevOps)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta: Marta here.
[00:08] Ethan: Ethan, on infra.
[00:10] Priya: Priya for security.
[00:11] Aaron: Aaron.
[00:12] Samir: Great, quick agenda — network follow-ups from the last run, runtime upgrade plan, tail latency review, and then action items. Jessica, Diego are you good to lead the benchmarks piece?
[00:24] Jessica: Yep I'll take benchmarks. We pulled the trace logs from last Thursday's run and saw a couple of spikes aligned to routing retries. Looks like a subset of requests were hitting a cross-AZ path because the peering rule for the staging VPC was still defaulting to the transit gateway route.
[00:41] Ethan: Yeah we changed the peering on Friday but I think the route table didn't propagate to one of the private subnets, so a few nodes were NAT-ing out then back in and that added like 60–120 ms to a small percentage of tokens.
[00:56] Marta: That explains the tail. Our SLO is 100 ms p95, 500 ms p99 — those spikes pushed us near p99 breach for a couple of tests.
[01:10] Diego: Right, we instrumented KV cache hits — cache hit-rate stayed high but the external routing caused the extra RTT. Also noticed connection churn when the runtime was on v2.1.4 during the long sequences.
[01:25] Jessica: This is why we recommended the v2.2.0-rc1 build, it's got a couple of improvements for persistent keepalive and reduced per-connection setup. It's still a release candidate but we've run it in a handful of pilot clusters.
[01:40] Priya: From security perspective, we're cautious about RCs. We need the security bundle and the exact KMS integration pattern — whether keys remain in our account or if Redwood can manage keys.
[01:53] Samir: Understood. We'll send the SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc after the call. For keys, our standard private deployment lets you manage keys in your KMS — Redwood's control plane doesn't have access to plaintext.
[02:08] Aaron: Quick question on audit logs — we need request-level logs with tokenized identifiers and a 90-day retention window. Is that supported in the private flow?
[02:18] Diego: Yes, the private package streams audit logs to your CloudWatch/Splunk endpoint; retention is on your side. The only caveat is performance if you enable synchronous logging for every request — we recommend batched asynchronous exports for production.
[02:33] Marta: Can you share the manifest for log fields so we can validate with compliance?
[02:36] Diego: Absolutely, I'll attach the manifest.
[02:39] Jessica: Back to the network — Samir can you confirm the peering checklist? I put a note in the shared deck but want to double-check NAT rules and security group flows.
[02:49] Samir: Yep, checklist is: create peering between customer-VPC and redwood-private-VPC, add route table entry for target CIDRs, ensure security groups allow 10.0/16 (example) and open port 443 to Redwood nodes, optional private link if they want a non-internet path. We also recommended a health-checkable endpoint so the routing doesn't prefer an unhealthy AZ.
[03:12] Ethan: On that, we found a misconfigured health check on one NLB which caused some connections to failover to the transit gateway. We'll fix the NLB config and re-run.
[03:22] Jessica: Great. For the runtime upgrade plan, Diego can you walk through the canary?
[03:28] Diego: Sure — proposed rollout: start with 5% of traffic on the canary group, 30-min watch window for error and latency metrics, then 25%, then 100% if stable. Rollback plan is immediate auto-failback to previous runtime if error rate crosses 1% or p99 increases by 2x. We'll also keep an isolated group for long-sequence tests.
[03:50] Marta: How disruptive is the upgrade? Any cold-start or KV cache invalidation?
[03:54] Diego: There is a small KV cache warming effect on first requests; we mitigate with pre-warming steps in the canary. Cold-start latency should be nominal; v2.2 added persistent keepalives to reduce handshake overhead.
[04:09] Aaron: Can we schedule the canary during our low traffic window 02:00–04:00 UTC?
[04:12] Samir: Yes we can do that. Jessica, can you run the latency benchmark matching their production sequences?
[04:20] Jessica: We'll run a focused 1-hour latency bench, emphasize p99 tail, and include long sequences up to 2k tokens. I'll need access to the staging route table and a short NAT exception window to avoid transit gateway fallback.
[04:33] Ethan: We'll give that window and confirm CIDRs.
[04:36] Priya: One more security ask — can Redwood sign the AAD/SSO flow with SAML assertions and map groups to RBAC roles? We want least privilege.
[04:46] Samir: Yes, SAML SSO is supported; we map SAML group attributes to roles. We'll send the mapping doc.
[04:52] Marta: On benchmarks, there was also a small increase in token cost on the long runs; is that from retries or additional compute?
[04:59] Diego: Mostly retries and the NAT-ing out/in added extra network egress cost; compute per token is constant aside from longer sequence memory pressure which can increase slightly. We can provide a cost breakout per run.
[05:12] Jessica: I'll attach the benchmark csv to the thread, it's linked in the shared doc — note the p99 spike at 520 ms in run 3 which aligns with the routing issue.
[05:22] Aaron: For the VPC peering, are there any IP overlap issues we should watch for?
[05:26] Samir: Avoid overlapping CIDRs, and if overlap exists we can negotiate a private link or use SNATing. Overlap causes asymmetric routing which triggers connection resets.
[05:37] Priya: About KMS — we need to be explicit that Redwood never holds plaintext; can you provide an architecture diagram?
[05:44] Diego: Yes, we'll add a diagram showing envelope encryption with customer KMS in your account.
[05:49] Marta: Quick recap before we wrap?
[05:51] Samir: Recap: Redwood to share network runbook and peering checklist, Diego to share runtime rollout notes and log manifest, Jessica to run latency benchmark on 2026-12-06, customer to confirm CIDRs and provide temporary NAT rule window, Redwood to share security bundle and SAML mapping doc.
[06:14] Marta: Sounds good.
[06:16] Samir: Any blockers?
[06:18] Ethan: None on infra once we fix the NLB health check.
[06:21] Priya: Waiting on the security bundle and log fields.
[06:24] Samir: We'll get those today. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread and meet next week.

Links referenced: shared doc: https://redwood.example.com/poc/atlas/notes, benchmark csv: https://sheets.example.com/atlas-bench-2026-11-30.csv

End of transcript.
